section.sectionSummaryBrief: This section contains the opening header and date of the maamar.
section.t: B"S.
Fourth day of the week, Parshat Beha'alotecha,
15 Sivan 5734*

section.sectionSummaryBrief: This section explains the distinction between the "lamps" mentioned in "when you raise up the lamps" and the "seven lamps" that shall give light, relating them to souls and the luminaries of the firmament.
section.t: "When you raise up the lamps, toward the face of the menorah shall the seven lamps give light."
And the Rebbe, my father-in-law, the leader of the captivity and the redemption, precisely notes in his maamar beginning with the words "Zeh" (this),
that first it says "when you raise up the lamps"
(lamps, without specification)
and does not mention their number,
and after this it says "shall the seven lamps give light."
And also one must understand
what is written "toward the face of the menorah shall the seven lamps give light,"
for the face of the menorah is the middle lamp,
and it should have said "toward the face of the menorah shall the six lamps give light."
And the point of the explanation of this is,
that the lamps about which it is said "when you raise up the lamps,"
and the lamps about which it is said "shall the seven lamps give light,"
are two matters.
"When you raise up the lamps,"
lamps without specification,
are the souls which are called lamps, as it is written,
"The lamp of Hashem is the soul of man."
For just as the nature of a flame is to ascend upward and cleave to its source
(in the general fire-element that is beneath the sphere
of the moon),
so too the soul has a natural ratzo (yearning) to ascend upward to be included in its source of hewing.
However, in the souls of Biyah (Creation, Formation, Action),
the nature of ratzo within them is in concealment,
and the service of Aharon is to arouse and reveal their natural ratzo and ascent,
"when you raise up the lamps,"
so that the nature of ascent within them will be revealed.
And "shall the seven lamps give light" refers to the luminaries in the firmament of the heavens,
as it is brought in the Midrash,
that the Mishkan is equivalent to the world,
for all the matters that were in the creation of the world had their counterpart in the Mishkan,
and the menorah that was in the Mishkan is the counterpart of "Let there be
luminaries in the firmament of the heavens."
And what is written "shall the seven lamps give light,"
even though in the statement "Let there be luminaries" it is written
"And Elokim made the two great luminaries etc.,"
this is,
because the sun and moon are the primary luminaries,
but in detail there are seven luminaries.
And this is "when you raise up the lamps... shall the seven lamps give light,"
that through the service of Aharon to raise up the lamps,
so that the souls of Biyah will have ratzo for Elokus in revelation,
through this "shall the seven lamps give light,"
that an addition of light is made in the utterance
"Let there be luminaries,"
in the manner of Sarah who added to the luminaries.

section.sectionSummaryBrief: This section explains that the lamps of the souls are the inner aspect of the lamps of the menorah, and questions the reason for the change in language between the two types of lamps.
section.t: B)
And behold, from this that "when you raise up the lamps" according to its simple meaning refers to the lamps of the menorah,
it is understood,
that this that "when you raise up the lamps" in the inner aspect of the matters refers to the souls, is because the lamps of the souls are the inner aspect of the lamps of the menorah.
[For in addition to this that the souls are lamps in general,
they are the lamps of the menorah.]
And this that in the menorah there were seven lamps is because the lamps of the souls are divided into seven types.
And based on this, one must understand the reason for the change in the language of the verse,
that regarding the lamps of the luminaries it is written "shall the seven lamps give light" and regarding the lamps of the souls it is written "when you raise up the lamps,"
lamps without specification.
